jamie: first-light handoff — quick summary of overnight
jamie: pages started ~04:12 UTC: KV prefix cache thrash on region-eu causing backend 503s and elevated p95 for chat/generation routes. Pager hit primary at 04:13.
jamie: root cause (current suspicion): heavy burst of similar long-context requests from a single customer -> KV K/V cache growth + regen thrash + eviction storms. not 100% confirmed yet.
jamie: what we did overnight: 1) scaled batcher down for region-eu to reduce memory churn 2) enabled temporary prefix-caching-locks (see runbook) 3) rolled a fallback model variant for highest-latency customer 4) applied throttle rule for the offending API key at 04:45
jamie: customer impact: two customers (acme-inc, docflow) saw 5-20% 5xxs during the 04:12-04:50 window, and p95 token latency doubled for some requests. billing unaffected but UX degraded.
lee: thanks jamie. I validated logs — eviction spikes in kv-cache pod logs around 04:14:03 to 04:18:11, then a brief recovery after throttle. snippet from kv-cache logs:
lee: ```
2026-03-25T04:14:03Z kv-cache[pid=62] INFO evicting prefix: client=acme-inc size=120MB total_keys=1.2M
2026-03-25T04:14:04Z kv-cache[pid=62] WARN eviction-rate: 980/s ack_delay=12ms
2026-03-25T04:18:09Z kv-cache[pid=62] INFO eviction-stabilized n=0
```
lee: confirmed the autoscaler also briefly overshot; we changed the policy to avoid immediate upscales on eviction spikes.
ops-bot: Incident 20260325-KVTHRASH created. Sev: P2. Affected routes: /v1/generate, /v1/chat. Pages sent to: @jamie @lee @sara. Link: https://incidents.internal/20260325-KVTHRASH
sara: oncall notes — primary: jamie, secondary: lee. Overnight coverage gap note: between 02:00-05:00 UTC we had only one escalation-capable engineer (jamie) because mike was on PTO and lisa was in meetings. that's our coverage gap that lengthened on pages.
sara: action item: update rota so we have a backup for the 02-06 UTC window this week. pinging @mike and @lisa to confirm availability for future shifts.
mike: saw the mention — I can pick up a single backup slot tomorrow 02-06 UTC. can we add me to rotation for the next 2 weeks? :thumbsup:
lisa: I can do a one-off this weekend (03/28) if needed, but not weekdays. will coordinate with ops.
jamie: runbook pointers I used:
jamie: - KV cache runbook: https://playbook.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-thrash
jamie: - Throttle guide (API key emergency block): https://playbook.internal/runbooks/quick-throttle
jamie: commands run (for record):
jamie: ```bash
# block offending API key
./infractl rate-limit set --key=ak_acme_123 --qps=0.5 --reason="temp emerg throttle"

# scale batcher down
kubectl -n inference scale deploy/batcher-region-eu --replicas=2

# tail kv-cache logs
kubectl -n infra logs deploy/kv-cache-region-eu -f | sed -n '1,200p'
```
jamie: status now: system stable but p95 slightly above normal for some tail requests. we've left the throttle in place (qps 0.5) and rollback will hinge on customer throttling confirmation.
lee: customer outreach: I pinged acme-eng at 05:10; they confirmed they were running a large import job and will re-run some workloads with backoff. docflow ops said they saw transient errors and accepted the fallback variant.
lee: monitoring: set temporary alert for eviction-rate > 500/s sustained > 2m to avoid regression. dashboard dash: https://grafana.internal/d/kv-cache
sara: next steps for the oncoming shift (actionable):
1) confirm with acme whether they want throttle lifted — contact acme-eng on #cust-acme or email acme-sre@acme.com
2) keep throttle for 1-2h after acme confirms backoff, then gradually increase qps by 0.25 steps while watching eviction rate
3) if eviction reappears, run fallback model rollout (see rollout runbook) and escalate to infra/eng-runtime
4) file post-incident note in /incidents with link and timeline (whoever takes next shift)
sara: coverage handoff: primary for next 12h: lee. secondary: lisa (on-call backup). jamie will remain reachable for quick questions until 10:00 UTC.
sara: please ack in-thread when you pick up the shift. also note the rota needs quick edit: add mike as backup for two morning slots per mike's offer.
lee: ack — taking primary. I'll follow the checklist, will check the eviction alert and customer comms first.
lisa: ack backup, available if pager hits escalation.
mike: ack on being added to rota, will update calendar.
jamie: last note — we should consider a mitigation engineering task: add prefix-size cap + early-drop for single-api-key rapid-growth patterns. filed task JT-4321 for next sprint.
jamie: end of handoff. :wave: please include any additional logs or notes in-thread so the next oncall has full context."
